title: Jacketed Vessel

introduction.definition: A jacketed vessel has an outer jacket around its lower shell. Steam, hot oil or cooling water flows through the jacket space and heats or cools the contents through the vessel wall. A spiral baffle in the jacket makes the medium flow fast around the vessel for good heat transfer.
applications: Batch heating/cooling in chemicals, food and pharma
key_points: No contact between medium and product
Jacket pressure acts externally on the shell
Heat transfer limited by wall area
introduction.summary: A jacketed vessel has an outer jacket around the lower part of the vessel. A heating or cooling medium (steam, hot oil, chilled water) flows through the jacket space and heats or cools the contents through the vessel wall without mixing with them. A spiral baffle guides the medium for better heat transfer.

alignment: Check verticality (vertical vessels) or level and slope (horizontal); one saddle bolted, the other slotted for thermal expansion.

video_tutorials.title: Jacketed Vessel — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Jacketed Vessel.
A jacketed vessel has an outer jacket around its lower shell.
Steam, hot oil or cooling water flows through the jacket space and heats or cools the contents through the vessel wall.
A spiral baffle in the jacket makes the medium flow fast around the vessel for good heat transfer.
Typical applications include batch heating/cooling in chemicals, food and pharma; melting and holding tanks; crystallisers and reactors; storage of temperature-sensitive products.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Jacketed Vessel — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Jacketed Vessel.
Check jacket steam trap and temperatures.
Descale jacket; inspect inner surface.
Hydro-test both spaces.
Watch for poor heating: long batch times. Common cause: air/condensate in jacket, scale.
Watch for inner shell buckling: deformation. Common cause: excess jacket pressure / vacuum inside.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
